paras: The threatened lynching at Flovilla was an attempt planned in August 1888 by white neighbors in Flovilla, Georgia, to lynch an unnamed Black man accused of assaulting his employer's 10-year-old daughter. Sheriff Beauchamp learned of the plan and carried the prisoner to Atlanta for safe keeping, and the episode survives in a single paragraph of Georgia news.

According to the report, the accused was a Black man employed by a white man at Flovilla. He was charged with having committed what the paper called "a terrible outrage" on his employer's 10-year-old daughter at sundown "one night last week," placing the alleged assault in mid-August 1888.

The child's mother was said to have frightened the man away, but he returned for supper, when she confronted him with a shotgun and told him "the slightest move would be a signal for his death." She kept him seated under guard for several hours until her husband came home at 10 o'clock, and continued to watch him while the husband gathered a number of neighbors to help take him to jail.
The neighbors, the paper said, "were so indignant that they were going to attempt to lynch him." Sheriff Beauchamp "got wind of it" and removed the prisoner to Atlanta before any attempt was made.
No report of an indictment, trial or later outcome for the accused man was found, and neither he nor the family was named.

The Savannah Morning News ran the account on August 21, 1888, as an unheadlined paragraph in its column of Georgia briefs, between a judge's career notice and a Blakely murder. The item stated the accusation as fact, gave most of its space to the mother's armed vigil, and described the lynching plan as the product of the neighbors' indignation without comment. No version of the episode in any other paper was found.

reader.title: Threatened lynching at Flovilla, Georgia (1888)
bases: Neighbors who helped take an accused Black man to jail 'were going to attempt to lynch him' before the sheriff moved him to Atlanta, a threatened lynching that was averted (A1).

No one was killed: the neighbors' planned lynching was forestalled when Sheriff Beauchamp carried the prisoner to Atlanta (A1). The threat was by 'a number of neighbors' acting on an accusation of rape, so it is a threatened lynching only.
The episode rests on one news-briefs paragraph in the Savannah Morning News, with no follow-up found (A1).

accounts.label: Georgia news-briefs item (Savannah Morning News)
accounts.gist: A Black employee committed an outrage on his employer's daughter, was held by her mother with a shotgun, and was taken to Atlanta by the sheriff after indignant neighbors planned to lynch him.

framing.detail: An unheadlined paragraph among Georgia briefs that states the accusation as fact ('committed a terrible outrage'), dwells on the armed mother's vigil, and reports the lynching plan as the neighbors' indignation without comment.

record_check.dossier: The article names no county; Butts is an inference from Flovilla's location, not stated in the report
One threatened person: an unnamed Black man employed by a white man at Flovilla
Neighbors gathered by the girl's father to guard the man to jail
Threat of lynching by neighbors; the 'armed' element in the article is the mother's shotgun guard, not the neighbors

record_check.record: the child's mother held him at gunpoint until her husband returned
record_check.dossier: Supported; note the man had left after the mother frightened him and returned for supper, when she held him

info: 'One night last week' before the August 21, 1888 report, i.e. about mid-August 1888; the alleged assault was at sundown
Threatened: an unnamed Black man ('a negro') employed by a white man at Flovilla
Accused of 'a terrible outrage' (rape) on his employer's 10-year-old daughter
Neighbors whom the father had gathered to guard the man to jail
Prisoner removed to Atlanta; no lynching; no report of a trial or later outcome was found

sources.note: Only report: unsigned paragraph in a Georgia news-briefs column; unnamed Black employee accused of an 'outrage' on his employer's 10-year-old daughter, held at shotgun point by the mother, neighbors planned a lynching, Sheriff Beauchamp took him to Atlanta.
quotes: a negro employed by a white man at that place, committed a terrible outrage on a 10-year-old daughter of his employer
the mother came in with a shotgun and told him that the slightest move would be a signal for his death
The neighbors were so indignant that they were going to attempt to lynch him, but Sheriff Beauchamp got wind of it and carried the prisoner to Atlanta for safe keeping.
